quote_orig: There is no question, to my mind, that ‘Mark is placing Jesus within the orbit of divine sovereignty and claiming a place for Jesus within the divine regency of “God Almighty”’, as Bird puts it, and that this is established “by way of reference to the Son of Man co-enthroned beside God and sharing in the visual marvel of the divine presence” (101).

claim_supported: (B) the Gospel writer (Mark) portrays Jesus as sharing YHWH's unique identity; not a claim about the historical Jesus's own words

The critic, who doubts Bird's wider claim that Mark identifies Jesus as the 'Lord' of Mark 1:3 (critic's earlier post), writes of this passage: 'There is no question, to my mind, that' Mark places Jesus within the orbit of divine sovereignty, yet the critic also says 'I summarise the arguments and set out my reasons for remaining unpersuaded.'
limits: Bird's book not opened. Quotation marks in the critic's text mark Bird's words; the surrounding sentence is the critic's.
